import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import bootstrap

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv')

# Filter the dataset for Business Analysts and Developers
business_analysts = df['Q8_ML_Addressing_Business_Analyst'].dropna()
developers = df['Q8_ML_Addressing_Developer'].dropna()

# Define a function to calculate the proportion
def proportion(data):
    return np.mean(data)

# Perform bootstrapping for Business Analysts
bootstrap_result_business_analysts = bootstrap((business_analysts,), proportion, confidence_level=0.95, random_state=123)

# Perform bootstrapping for Developers
bootstrap_result_developers = bootstrap((developers,), proportion, confidence_level=0.95, random_state=123)

# Get the results
proportion_business_analysts = bootstrap_result_business_analysts.statistic
ci_lower_business_analysts = bootstrap_result_business_analysts.confidence_interval[0]
ci_upper_business_analysts = bootstrap_result_business_analysts.confidence_interval[1]

proportion_developers = bootstrap_result_developers.statistic
ci_lower_developers = bootstrap_result_developers.confidence_interval[0]
ci_upper_developers = bootstrap_result_developers.confidence_interval[1]

proportion_business_analysts, ci_lower_business_analysts, ci_upper_business_analysts, proportion_developers, ci_lower_developers, ci_upper_developers
